GUPTA DYNASTY (320 AD-543 AD)

Gupta Dynasty (320 AD-543 AD)

  • Founder: Sri Gupta (Son: Ghatotkach)
  • Guptas ruled over Madhyadesha (Uttar Pradesh + Madhya Pradesh + Bihar).
  • They are considered to be feudatories of Kushans.
  • The Gupta age in ancient India has been called the "Golden Age of India" because of the many achievements in the field of arts, science, and literature that Indians made under the Guptas.

Chandragupta I (319 AD-335 AD)

  • Title: Maharajadhiraja
  • Married to: Kumaradevi (Lichchavi Princess)
  • He started Gupta Era in 320 AD/319 AD.
  • Gold coins introduced by him were called Dinars.

Samudragupta (335 AD-375 AD)

  • He was the most powerful and greatest king of the dynasty.
  • Record of his reign is mentioned in Prayag Prasasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription → Composed by Harisena (his court poet)).
  • Samudragupta is considered to have remained undefeated in battles.
  • He is titled "Napoleon of India" by V. A. Smith.
  • Other titles taken: Param Bhagavat, Sarva-raj-ochchetta (uprooter of all king), Lichchavi dauhitra
  • He has been shown playing Veena on coins.
  • He performed Ashwamedha Yagya.
  • Samudragupta granted permission to Meghavarman, the Buddhist king of Ceylon (Sri Lanka) to build a monastery in Bodh Gaya.

Chandragupta II (380 AD-415 AD)

  • He achieved power by assassinating his brother Ramgupta and Saka invader.
  • He married his brother's wife Dhruvadevi.
  • He formed matrimonial alliance by marrying off his daughter Prabhavati Gupta with Vakataka Prince Rudrasena II.
  • He was the first Gupta to introduce Silver coins after the victory over Sakas (this is mentioned in Mehrauli Iron Pillar in Delhi).
  • He took the title Vikramaditya after defeating Sakas.
  • Indirectly ruled by Guptas after death of Rudrasena II (his wife ascended the throne)

Navratnas of Chandragupta II

  • His court was adorned with nine Navratnas. They were:
NameRole
AmarsimhaLexicographer
DhanvantriPhysician
HarisenaCourt poet
KalidasShakespeare of India
SankuArchitect
VarahamihiraAstronomer
VararuchiGrammarian, Sanskrit scholar
Vetala BhattaMagician
KshapanakaAstrologer
  • He was visited by Fa-Hien, the first Chinese traveller during his reign.

Books by Kalidas

  • Abhigyan Shakuntalam
  • Malvikagnimitra
  • Raghuvamsa
  • Meghadutta
  • Kumar Sambhavam
  • Ritusamhara
  • Amarsimha wrote "Amarkosh".
  • Vetala Bhatta wrote "Mantra Shastra".

Books by Sudraka

  • Mrichchhakatika: It is a love story of Charudatta and Vasantasena (also known as: The little clay art).

Kumaragupta I (415 AD-455 AD)

  • He was the son of Chandragupta II.
  • His empire was attacked by Huns.
  • He founded Nalanda University.
  • Mehrauli Iron Pillar

Skandagupta I (455 AD-467 AD)

  • He successfully resisted the attack of Huns.
  • Title taken: Vikramaditya (source: Bhitari Pillar Inscription)
  • He also repaired Sudarshan lake.
  • He moved his capital to Saketa and renamed it Ayodhya after the legendary city in the Ramayana.

Administration → Decentralised

  • Empire → Bhuktis (under the charge of Uparika)
  • Divided into districts
  • Vishayas (under the charge of Vishaya Patis)
  • Vithis (under the charge of Nagarpati)
  • Villages (under the charge of Gramika)

Important Officers

OfficerRole
KumaramatyasProvincial Officer (most important Officer)
Mahadanda NayakaOfficer responsible for punishment (Minister of Justice)
SandhivigrahikaThe officer of war and peace
Nagara ShresthiChief Banker of the city
Note: Harisena held all these posts except Nagara Shresthi

Economy

#### Taxes

TaxDescription
Bhaga1/6th of the produce to be paid by cultivators
BhogaPeriodic supplies of fruit, flowers to the King
BaliOppressive
UparikaraExtra tax
VishtiForm of forced labour
HalivarkaTo be paid by one who owned a plough
UdakabhagaTax on water
HirayanaTax for special purpose

Culture

  • Built by: Chandragupta II
  • Avatar of Lord Vishnu
  • Place: Udaygiri, Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh
  • Place: Deogarh, Lalitpur, Uttar Pradesh
  • Dedicated to Lord Krishna
  • It is also known as Brick Temple (one of the oldest)
  • Famous for ancient mural paintings
  • The first known inscriptional evidence of the practice of Sati in Bhanugupta, which dates back to the 5th Century CE

VAKATAKA DYNASTY

  • Founder: Vindhyashakti
  • They were feudatories of Satavahanas.
  • They were the contemporaries of Guptas.
  • They followed Brahmanism but also patronised Buddhism.
  • They ruled in the Central and Southern part of India.
  • In Puranas, they have been mentioned as Vindhyakas.
  • The rock-cut Buddhist Viharas and Chaityas of Ajanta Caves were built under the patronage of Vakataka king, Harisena.
  • Total Puranas: 18
  • Written by: Sage Vyasa
  • Compiled by: 3rd-10th Century AD
